title: Invite flow hardening and tenant email controls
creator: Ava Kline
description:
Goal: Deliver a hardened organization invite flow and tenant-level email controls (allowlist/denylist + domain verification) that integrate with RBAC v2, produce actionable audit logs, and play nicely with SSO/SAML-managed tenants. This ticket coordinates the API, console UI, backend enforcement, migration for existing tenants, and automated tests.

Problem statement: Existing invite behavior allows some ambiguous edge cases for tenants using SSO or with domain controls enabled. Admins need deterministic policies (block invites, require verification, require SSO enrollment) and clear audit records for every invite lifecycle event. RBAC v2 introduces granular admin roles which must be respected by invite policies.

Scope:
- Backend: invite policy engine (tenant-level settings), domain verification state machine, allowlist/denylist enforcement at invite acceptance and API invite endpoints, SSO-aware invite behaviors.
- Console: new Admin -> Org settings page sections for Invite Policy, Verified Domains, and Email Allow/Deny lists with CSV import and per-row comments.
- API: stable endpoints for reading/updating tenant invite policies, endpoints for verifying domains (DNS/TXT flow + verification webhook), and audit events for all operations.
- Telemetry & Audit: structured audit logs for: invite_created, invite_sent, invite_accepted, invite_revoked, domain_verified, domain_revoked, allowlist_updated. Logs must include actor, actor_role, target_email, target_domain, tenant_id, policy_snapshot_id, request_id, and timestamp.
- Migration: backfill domain verification status from existing domain verification attempts, and default policies for tenants with SSO enabled.

Out of scope: per-user granular allowlists beyond tenant-level controls, federation of domain verification across multiple tenants (future RFC).
acceptance_criteria: Tenant admins can set Invite Policy to: allow_all, email_allowlist_only, email_denylist_block, require_domain_verified, require_sso; setting is enforced by API and console
Domain verification flow implemented: TXT DNS token issuance, verification webhook handler, and UI feedback with 48-hour verification TTL and re-issue capability
Email allowlist/denylist supports CSV import, 10k rows paginated editing, and wildcard domain entries (e.g., @acme.com); enforcement checks at invite creation and invite acceptance
RBAC v2 checks performed at all admin API endpoints: only roles with org.admin or org.security_admin can modify policy or verified domains
Structured audit logs emitted for all invite and domain actions and stored in audit pipeline with retention tag for enterprise customers
Automated tests: unit tests for policy engine, integration tests for invite API with SSO tenant, e2e test for UI flows
Migration script to set sane defaults for existing tenants and a dry-run mode for ops
Feature rollout gated behind runtime flag 'invite_policy_v2' and gradual rollout with telemetry verifying <0.1% error rate before enabling for all tenants
implementation_notes: Policy engine design: declarative policy objects (policy_version, rules list) to allow future extension (rate limits, rate-limited invites, conditional SSO enforcement)
Enforcement points: Admin Console (client-side validation + server-side enforcement), REST API /orgs/:id/invites, incoming invite accept endpoint /invites/accept
Domain verification: reuse existing verification service but add verification 'owner' field and per-tenant token namespace to avoid cross-tenant collisions

SSO interactions: tenants with SAML SSO configured should have default 'require_sso' policy; invites to emails not associated with SSO assertion should be blocked or routed to a 'request access' flow depending on tenant config
Audit format: JSONL records keyed by event_type; include policy_snapshot_id to allow forensic reconstruction of decision logic at time of event
RBAC v2 impact: add new permission 'org.manage_invite_policies' and ensure migration maps legacy org.owner to new permission for backward compatibility
Rate limiting: invite API must respect per-tenant soft bursts; add server-side throttling and clear 429 error messages that indicate policy conflict vs. rate limit
UI: editable allowlist with preview of effective policy for a sample email; warn admins when wildcard entries produce broad matches
